family_title: Adapter modules and side networks (architectural insertion)

methods.name: Residual Adapters
methods.full_name: Residual adapter modules for multi-domain ResNets
methods.paper_title: Learning multiple visual domains with residual adapters
methods.formula_latex: g(x;\alpha) = x + \alpha * x,\quad \alpha\in\mathbb{R}^{C\times C\times 1\times 1}\ (\text{bank of }1{\times}1\text{ filters, wrapped with domain-specific BN});\quad \text{frozen: domain-agnostic }3{\times}3\text{ filters } w_1,w_2;\ \text{trained per domain: } \alpha,\ \text{BN scale/shift}
methods.trainable_params: 2(C^2+5C)\ \text{per residual block (vs. } 2(h^2C^2+hC)\text{ shared, } h=3)
methods.locus: inside every ResNet residual block, in series after each 3x3 convolution (with batch-norm)
methods.structure: Serial insertion of a linear near-identity endomorphism I+\alpha of the C-channel feature space (a per-pixel C\times C matrix, i.e. 1x1 conv) composed with domain-specific BN affine maps; full-rank, no bottleneck, no nonlinearity. The CVPR 2018 follow-up (Rebuffi et al., arXiv:1803.10082) moves the 1x1 adapter in parallel to the 3x3 convolution.
methods.mergeable_reason: At inference every piece is linear or affine: BN, the 1x1 adapter I+\alpha and the BN that follows sit between a frozen 3x3 convolution and the ReLU (Fig. 2). They therefore fold exactly into a domain-specific 3x3 filter bank plus bias (per tap W' = D_2(I+\alpha D_1)W). The paper keeps them unmerged so that one backbone is shared across domains.
methods.identity_at_init: Exactly the identity when \alpha=0 (residual form); in the paper adapters are first co-trained with the backbone on ImageNet, then only domain-specific parameters (with strong weight decay on \alpha) are trained per domain.
methods.key_idea: Split a multi-domain ResNet into frozen domain-agnostic filters plus tiny domain-specific residual 1x1 adapters that collapse to the identity at zero, so one network can be steered across very different visual domains; this is the origin of the term 'adapter' later imported to NLP by Houlsby et al.
methods.results_note: On the Visual Decathlon (10 image domains) residual adapters adding ~11% parameters per domain are close to or better than full per-domain fine-tuning while avoiding forgetting.
methods.verification_notes: Checked against the arXiv PDF (v5): title, authors, NIPS 2017 venue, g(x;\alpha)=x+\alpha*x with 1x1 filters, BN placement, the 2(C^2+5C) domain-specific parameter count and the ~11% per-domain overhead (Sec. 3.2, 5).
corrections: mergeable: 'conditional' -> 'yes'. Every merge yields a task-specific weight, so needing a per-domain copy is not a condition. The adapter (BN, then 1x1 conv with skip, then BN) sits between the frozen 3x3 conv and the ReLU (paper Fig. 2), so it folds exactly.

Removed relation 'competes-with repadapter'. The two methods are six years apart, RepAdapter does not cite Rebuffi et al., and they do not compete. The structural link is now described in repadapter.structure.

methods.name: Adapter (Houlsby)
methods.full_name: Bottleneck adapter modules (serial, two per layer)
methods.paper_title: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for NLP
methods.formula_latex: y = F(x)\ (\text{frozen sublayer after its output projection});\quad y \leftarrow y + W_{up}\,\sigma(W_{down}\,y + b_{down}) + b_{up};\quad \text{then } \mathrm{LN}(x+y);\quad W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{trained (plus LayerNorm and head); all pretrained weights frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2\,(2rd + r + d)\ \text{per layer (two adapters)} + \text{LayerNorm parameters}
methods.locus: two serial adapters per Transformer layer: after the attention output projection and after the FFN, each before the residual add and LayerNorm
methods.structure: Bottleneck MLP inserted serially with an internal residual connection: each frozen sublayer F is post-composed with the near-identity endomorphism \mathrm{id}+W_{up}\sigma W_{down} of \mathbb{R}^d (rank-r bottleneck, nonlinear).
methods.mergeable_reason: The nonlinearity inside the bottleneck prevents folding the adapter into the frozen linear weights, so inference keeps the extra sequential modules and latency.
methods.identity_at_init: Near-identity, not exact. Projection weights are drawn from a zero-mean Gaussian with std 10^{-2} truncated at 2 std, and biases are zero, so the adapter output is close to 0 and the internal skip makes the module approximately the identity. The paper's init-scale sweep finds performance robust for std <= 10^{-2} and degrading for larger scales.
methods.key_idea: Insert small bottleneck modules with a skip connection into every Transformer layer and train only them (plus LayerNorms), so one frozen BERT serves many tasks with a few percent new parameters per task.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with BERT-Large, adapters reach a mean score of 80.0 vs 80.4 for full fine-tuning while adding 3.6% parameters per task, and remain competitive across 26 text-classification tasks.

relations.note: Transfers Rebuffi et al.'s residual adapter idea to Transformers, adding a bottleneck and a nonlinearity.
Serial (post-composition) vs parallel (sum with the sublayer) insertion of the same bottleneck module, as analysed by He et al. (2022).
Main alternative PEFT family; LoRA is a linear, parallel, mergeable update.

methods.verification_notes: arXiv/ICML 2019 confirmed. The paper states 2md+d+m parameters per adapter, two serial adapters per layer after the output projection and before the skip-add and LayerNorm, LayerNorm parameters trained, and truncated N(0,1e-4) init. The GLUE numbers (80.0 vs 80.4, 3.6%) match the paper.
corrections: identity_at_init: replaced 'training can fail if init deviates too far' with the paper's actual finding (Sec. 3.6, Fig. 6): robust for std <= 1e-2, degrading for larger init scales.

methods.name: Pfeiffer Adapter
methods.paper_title: AdapterFusion: Non-Destructive Task Composition for Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: a = \mathrm{LN}\big(x + F(x)\big)\ (F = \text{frozen FFN sublayer, LN its frozen post-LayerNorm});\quad y = W_{up}\,\mathrm{ReLU}(W_{down}\,a + b_{down}) + b_{up} + F(x);\quad h = \mathrm{LN}(y + x);\quad W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{trained; backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2rd + r + d\ \text{per layer (one adapter; default reduction factor } d/r = 16)
methods.locus: one adapter per Transformer layer, only after the feed-forward block
methods.structure: Same algebraic shape as the Houlsby adapter (serial residual bottleneck MLP) but inserted once per layer, after the FFN, with the residual taken from the FFN sublayer; found by an architecture search over positions, residuals, LayerNorms, reduction factors and nonlinearities.
methods.mergeable_reason: Nonlinear bottleneck in series with the FFN cannot be absorbed into frozen weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Approximate only. The paper adds 'randomly initialized' adapters, and the AdapterHub default (init_weights='bert') is N(0, 0.02^2) weights with zero biases. The bottleneck output is small but not zero, and there is no exact zero-init guarantee.
methods.key_idea: A single adapter after the FFN performs on par with Houlsby's two adapters per layer while halving the inserted modules and compute; it became the default sequential adapter (SeqBnConfig) of AdapterHub and the building block of AdapterFusion and MAD-X.
methods.results_note: In the paper's architecture search on SST-2, CommonsenseQA and argument mining, the single post-FFN adapter matched the Houlsby configuration with half as many adapters.

relations.note: Keeps only the FFN-side adapter of the Houlsby design.

methods.verification_notes: Single post-FFN adapter found by an architecture search on SST-2, CSQA and Argument (AdapterFusion App. A.2). EACL 2021 confirmed via arXiv journal-ref. Default reduction factor 16 confirmed in AdapterHub SeqBnConfig.
corrections: formula_latex: made the residual explicit. MAD-X Eq. 1 defines r_l as the output of the FFN and h_l as the output of the following LayerNorm. AdapterHub SeqBnConfig (original_ln_before/after=True, residual_before_ln=True) computes LN(W_up ReLU(W_down LN(x+F(x))) + F(x) + x). The earlier text 'rho = residual of the FFN sublayer' was ambiguous.
identity_at_init: the init is now attributed to AdapterHub's default ('bert', std 0.02). The paper only says 'randomly initialized'.

methods.name: MAD-X
methods.full_name: Multiple ADapters for Cross-lingual transfer (language, task and invertible adapters)
methods.paper_title: MAD-X: An Adapter-Based Framework for Multi-Task Cross-Lingual Transfer
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{LA}_l(h_l,\rho_l) = U_l\,\mathrm{ReLU}(D_l h_l) + \rho_l,\quad \mathrm{TA}_l(h_l,\rho_l) = U'_l\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(D'_l\,\mathrm{LA}_l(h_l,\rho_l)\big) + \rho_l;\quad A_{inv}:\ o_1 = F(e_2)+e_1,\ o_2 = G(o_1)+e_2,\ \ A_{inv}^{-1}:\ e_2 = o_2 - G(o_1),\ e_1 = o_1 - F(e_2);\ \ F,G\ \text{bottleneck MLPs};\ \text{backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: \underbrace{2r_Ld}_{\text{language}} + \underbrace{2r_Td}_{\text{task}}\ \text{per layer} + \underbrace{\tfrac{d^2}{2}}_{\text{invertible (once)}}\ (\text{+ biases; paper: } r_L = d/2,\ r_T = d/16)
methods.locus: language and task adapters stacked after the FFN in every layer; invertible adapter on the input embeddings with its inverse before the tied output embeddings
methods.structure: Serial composition (stacking) TA\circ LA of two bottleneck adapters that share the FFN residual, plus an invertible NICE additive-coupling bijection A_{inv} on token embeddings whose exact inverse is applied before the tied output embedding; language modules are swappable at inference (zero-shot transfer by replacing LA^{src} with LA^{tgt}).
methods.mergeable_reason: Nonlinear bottlenecks and coupling layers must be executed at inference; swapping modules is the point of the design.
methods.identity_at_init: Not explicitly enforced: adapters use the standard small random init of Pfeiffer adapters; the coupling A_{inv} equals the identity only when F=G=0.
methods.key_idea: Factor cross-lingual transfer into separately trained, swappable language adapters (MLM on unlabeled text), task adapters stacked on top, and invertible embedding adapters, so a task adapter trained in one language transfers zero-shot to another by swapping the language adapter.
methods.results_note: With XLM-R Base, full MAD-X improves over XLM-R by more than 5 F1 on average for cross-lingual NER (largest gains on low-resource and unseen languages) and is competitive on XQuAD.

relations.note: Language and task adapters use the Pfeiffer architecture.
Alternative way to compose adapters: stacking/swapping instead of attention-based fusion.

methods.verification_notes: Eqs. for LA, TA and the NICE invertible adapter match the paper (Sec. 4.1-4.3). F and G use D in R^{h/4 x h/2}, which gives h^2/2 invertible parameters. Default dims 384/192/48 for XLM-R Base give ~8.25M per language (paper Table 5). EMNLP 2020 confirmed.

methods.name: AdapterFusion
methods.full_name: AdapterFusion: attention-based composition of task adapters
methods.paper_title: AdapterFusion: Non-Destructive Task Composition for Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: s_{l,t} = \mathrm{softmax}_{n}\big(h_{l,t}^{\top}Q_l \cdot z_{l,t,n}^{\top}K_l\big),\quad z'_{l,t,n} = z_{l,t,n}^{\top}V_l,\quad o_{l,t} = \sum_{n=1}^{N} s_{l,t,n}\,z'_{l,t,n};\quad \text{frozen: backbone and } N \text{ trained task adapters } \Phi_n;\ \text{trained: } Q_l,K_l,V_l\ (\text{and head})
methods.trainable_params: 3d^2 + 3d\ \text{per layer}\ (Q_l,K_l,V_l\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times d})
methods.locus: a fusion layer after the N parallel task adapters at the FFN position of every layer
methods.structure: Input-dependent convex combination: a dot-product attention whose query is the FFN output and whose keys/values are the outputs of N frozen adapters, i.e. a context-dependent point of the simplex \Delta^{N-1} mixing V-projected adapter outputs (two-stage: knowledge extraction, then composition).
methods.mergeable_reason: All N adapters and the attention mixer run at inference; the mixing weights depend on the input.
methods.identity_at_init: No: Q and K are random; V is initialized to an identity diagonal plus 1e-6 noise (and L2-regularized toward it), so at init the layer outputs an attention-weighted average of adapter outputs, not the base model.
methods.key_idea: Separate knowledge extraction (train one adapter per task, non-destructively) from knowledge composition (learn a small attention layer that mixes the frozen adapters per token for a target task), avoiding catastrophic forgetting and task interference of multi-task fine-tuning.
methods.results_note: Across 16 NLU tasks with BERT-base, AdapterFusion improves over full fine-tuning and over single-task and multi-task adapters on the target task.

relations.note: Fuses single-task Pfeiffer adapters.
Both mix several adapters per layer; AdaMix routes stochastically and averages weights instead of attending over outputs.

methods.verification_notes: Fusion attention softmax(h^T Q . z^T K) with value projection z^T V matches Sec. 3.2. V is initialized to an identity diagonal plus 1e-6 noise and L2-regularized (Sec. 4.3). 3d^2+3d assumes biased d x d Q/K/V, as in the AdapterHub implementation. EACL 2021 confirmed.

methods.name: AdapterDrop
methods.full_name: AdapterDrop: dropping adapters from lower Transformer layers
methods.paper_title: AdapterDrop: On the Efficiency of Adapters in Transformers
methods.formula_latex: h^{(l)} = \begin{cases} F_l\big(h^{(l-1)}\big) & l \le n \\ A_l\big(F_l(h^{(l-1)})\big) & l > n \end{cases},\qquad n \text{ fixed (specialized) or } n\sim\mathcal{U}\{0,\dots,11\}\ \text{per batch (robust)};\ \text{backbone frozen, adapters } A_l \text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: (L-n)\,(2rd + r + d)\ \text{for specialized AdapterDrop (adapters only in the top } L-n \text{ layers)};\ L\,(2rd+r+d)\ \text{for robust AdapterDrop (all adapters trained, } n \text{ resampled per batch)}
methods.locus: adapters kept only in the upper L-n layers; the first n layers are the unmodified backbone
methods.structure: Restricts the set of insertion sites to a final segment of the layer chain, so the composite factors as (adapted top) \circ (shared frozen bottom); the shared prefix can be computed once for many tasks. The robust variant samples n per batch (stochastic depth over adapters). Also prunes AdapterFusion to its most-attended adapters.
methods.mergeable_reason: Remaining adapters are ordinary nonlinear bottleneck adapters.
methods.identity_at_init: Inherited from the underlying adapter initialization (approximate identity); the first n layers are exactly the backbone.
methods.key_idea: Lower layers matter little for adapters, so removing their adapters (during training and/or inference) speeds up training and multi-task inference with small accuracy loss; one robustly trained model can be run with any number of dropped layers.
methods.results_note: With RoBERTa-base on GLUE, dropping adapters from the first five layers keeps 97.1% (specialized) / 95.4% (robust) of performance and makes simultaneous inference on 8 tasks 39% faster; pruning AdapterFusion from 8 to 2 adapters keeps performance.

relations.note: Applied to Pfeiffer and Houlsby adapters.
AdapterFusion pruning removes the least-activated adapters.

methods.verification_notes: Specialized/robust variants, n drawn from [0,11] per batch, 97.1%/95.4% retention with 5 dropped layers and 39% faster 8-task inference all match the paper. EMNLP 2021 confirmed via arXiv comment.
corrections: trainable_params: added the robust variant, which trains all L adapters with n ~ U[0,11] per batch (paper Sec. 3).

methods.name: K-Adapter
methods.paper_title: K-Adapter: Infusing Knowledge into Pre-Trained Models with Adapters
methods.formula_latex: a_k = \mathcal{A}_k\big([\,h_{l_k}\,;\,a_{k-1}\,]\big),\ \ \mathcal{A}_k = \text{down-proj} \to N\ \text{Transformer layers} \to \text{up-proj (skip across the projections)},\ \ l_k\in\{0,11,23\};\quad \text{output } [\,h_L\,;\,a_K\,];\quad \text{knowledge pre-training: backbone frozen, } \mathcal{A}\text{ trained}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 42\text{M per knowledge adapter during knowledge pre-training (RoBERTa-Large frozen; } K=3 \text{ adapter layers at backbone layers } \{0,11,23\},\ N=2,\ H_A=768,\ H_d=768,\ H_u=1024);\ \text{downstream fine-tuning updates RoBERTa with the adapters frozen}
methods.locus: outside plug-in (side network) reading hidden states of backbone layers {0, 11, 23}; its output is concatenated with the backbone's final hidden state
methods.structure: Side network: a separate small Transformer stack that reads (by concatenation) intermediate backbone states and never writes back into the backbone; the final representation is the concatenation (a product) of backbone and side-network features, and multiple knowledge adapters are combined by further concatenation.
methods.mergeable_reason: A separate network with its own Transformer layers runs alongside the backbone.
methods.identity_at_init: No: adapters are randomly initialized; the backbone representation is left untouched (outputs are concatenated, not added), so original features stay available but the head sees a new concatenated feature.
methods.key_idea: Inject different kinds of knowledge (factual relations from Wikidata, dependency syntax) into independent side adapters trained with the backbone frozen, enabling continual, non-interfering knowledge infusion. Note: for downstream tasks the paper keeps the adapters fixed and fine-tunes RoBERTa, so it is a modular knowledge-infusion method rather than a downstream PEFT method.
methods.results_note: K-Adapter (factual + linguistic) improves RoBERTa-Large on entity typing (OpenEntity +1.38 F1), relation classification and question answering.

relations.note: Concurrent side-network design; K-Adapter reads intermediate layers and fuses by concatenation.
Plugs adapters outside the backbone instead of inside each layer.

methods.verification_notes: Architecture (K adapter layers with N=2 Transformer layers, skip across projections, plug-in at {0,11,23}, concatenation fusion, ~42M parameters) matches Sec. 3.1. Venue confirmed via Crossref DOI 10.18653/v1/2021.findings-acl.121.
corrections: trainable_params: added the downstream regime. The paper (App. E) fixes the adapters and fine-tunes all of RoBERTa, so the ~42M figure applies only to knowledge pre-training.

methods.name: Compacter
methods.paper_title: Compacter: Efficient Low-Rank Hypercomplex Adapter Layers
methods.formula_latex: A^{l}(x) = \mathrm{LPHM}^{U^l}\big(\mathrm{GeLU}(\mathrm{LPHM}^{D^l}(x))\big) + x,\quad W = \sum_{i=1}^{n} A_i \otimes \big(s_i t_i^{\top}\big),\ \ A_i\in\mathbb{R}^{n\times n}\ \text{shared by all adapters},\ s_i\in\mathbb{R}^{d/n},\ t_i\in\mathbb{R}^{r/n}\ \text{per adapter};\ \text{backbone frozen (LayerNorms trained)}
methods.trainable_params: 2(d+r)\ \text{per adapter} + n^3\ \text{shared}\ \ (\text{total } 4L(d+r)+n^3 \text{ with two adapters per layer})
methods.locus: Houlsby positions (after attention and after FFN); Compacter++ keeps only the post-FFN adapter
methods.structure: Bottleneck adapter whose down/up matrices are parameterized hypercomplex multiplications: sums of n Kronecker products A_i\otimes B_i with globally shared 'slow' factors A_i and per-adapter rank-one 'fast' factors B_i = s_i t_i^{\top}; parameter cost O(d+r) instead of O(dr).
methods.mergeable_reason: Still a nonlinear serial bottleneck; the Kronecker structure only compresses its weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Not explicitly guaranteed in the paper; the residual form makes the module near-identity when the generated projections are small.
methods.key_idea: Compress adapter weights with parameterized hypercomplex (Kronecker-sum) layers whose small factors are shared across all layers and whose large factors are rank-one, reaching ~0.05% trainable parameters.
methods.results_note: With T5-base, Compacter (0.073%) and Compacter++ (0.047% of parameters) match full fine-tuning on GLUE and outperform it on SuperGLUE and in low-resource settings.

relations.note: Same adapter positions and residual bottleneck, with Kronecker-factored weights.
Compacter++ uses the single post-FFN placement.

methods.verification_notes: LPHM adapter, W = sum_i A_i (x) s_i t_i^T with A_i shared across all layers and positions, and the total 4L(k+d)+n^3 parameters match Sec. 3-4 (biases ignored, as in the paper). 0.073%/0.047% figures confirmed. NeurIPS 2021 confirmed.

methods.name: HyperFormer
methods.paper_title: Parameter-efficient Multi-task Fine-tuning for Transformers via Shared Hypernetworks
methods.formula_latex: A^{l}_{\tau}(x) = \mathrm{LN}^{l}_{\tau}\big(U^{l}_{\tau}\,\mathrm{GeLU}(D^{l}_{\tau}x)\big) + x,\quad (U^{l}_{\tau},D^{l}_{\tau}) = (W^{U},W^{D})\,I_{\tau},\ \ (\gamma^{l}_{\tau},\beta^{l}_{\tau}) = (W^{\gamma},W^{\beta})\,I_{\tau},\ \ I_{\tau} = h'_I(z_{\tau}, l_i, p_j)\ (\text{HyperFormer++});\ \text{backbone frozen except its LayerNorms}
methods.trainable_params: t(T+4+2L) + 8te + 2t(2dr + 2d)\ \text{in total for } T \text{ tasks (HyperFormer++, } t=64,\ e=128);\ \text{a new task adds } t
methods.locus: Houlsby positions (after attention and FFN blocks) in the T5 encoder and decoder, plus task-conditional LayerNorm inside adapters
methods.structure: Adapter weights are the image of a learned linear map (hypernetwork) applied to an embedding of (task, layer id, adapter position); all adapters therefore lie in a shared t-dimensional linear subspace of adapter-parameter space, with nonlinear adapters instantiated from it.
methods.mergeable_reason: Once a task embedding is fixed the generated module is an ordinary nonlinear bottleneck adapter, which cannot be folded into the frozen weights.
methods.identity_at_init: No exact guarantee: generated adapter weights are random at init (residual form gives approximate identity only if the generated weights are small).
methods.key_idea: Share knowledge across tasks by generating every task's adapter and conditional-LayerNorm parameters from one hypernetwork conditioned on task, layer and position embeddings, so adding a task costs only a task embedding.
methods.results_note: In multi-task GLUE with T5-base, HyperFormer++ scores 86.48 vs 84.88 for task-specific adapters with 0.29% trainable parameters per task, and improves few-shot domain generalization.

relations.note: Generates Houlsby-style adapters with a hypernetwork.
Same authors; parameter sharing via hypernetwork vs via shared Kronecker factors.

methods.verification_notes: Adapter A = LN_tau(U GeLU(D x)) + x, the linear hypernetworks (W^U, W^D) I_tau and the HyperFormer++ total t(T+4+2L)+8te+2t(2hd+2h) (t=64, e=128) match the paper (Sec. 2, 4.1). GLUE 86.48 vs 84.88 confirmed. ACL 2021 confirmed.

methods.name: Parallel Adapter
methods.paper_title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: h \leftarrow F(x) + s\cdot W_{up}\,\sigma(W_{down}\,x),\quad x = \text{input of the frozen sublayer } F\ (\text{FFN or attention});\ \ s=1\ (\text{PA}),\ s>1\ \text{fixed (scaled PA, e.g. } s=4);\ \ W_{down}\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d},\ W_{up}\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: 2rd\ (+\,r + d \text{ biases})\ \text{per adapted sublayer}
methods.locus: in parallel to the FFN (preferred) or attention sublayer, reading the sublayer input
methods.structure: Additive parallel composition: the frozen sublayer map F is replaced by F + s\,g with g = W_{up}\sigma W_{down} a bottleneck MLP of the same input (a sum of two morphisms with common domain), versus the serial post-composition (\mathrm{id}+g)\circ F of sequential adapters.
methods.mergeable_reason: The bottleneck is nonlinear and F (an FFN) is nonlinear, so F+sg cannot be rewritten as the original architecture; with \sigma = id around a single linear map it collapses to LoRA, which is mergeable.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact for the scaled PA as implemented: LoRA-style init (W_down Kaiming-uniform, W_up = 0), so the parallel branch outputs 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Viewing prefix tuning as a gated parallel adapter on attention outputs suggests moving adapters from serial to parallel insertion, placing them at the FFN, and borrowing LoRA's scaling; parallel insertion beats serial at equal budget (a similar parallel adapter was proposed concurrently by Zhu et al., 2021 for MT).
methods.results_note: On XSum summarization and WMT16 en-ro translation, the FFN parallel adapter outperforms the FFN sequential adapter by 1.7 ROUGE-2 and 0.8 BLEU at the same parameter budget.

relations.note: LoRA is a scaled parallel adapter around a single linear map with \sigma = identity.
He et al. show prefix tuning equals a softmax-gated parallel adapter on head outputs; PA transfers this insertion form.
Parallel vs serial insertion of the same bottleneck.

methods.verification_notes: PA/scaled PA (s=4 fixed, or trainable s) and the LoRA-style init used for scaled PA (App. A.3) are confirmed. PA(ffn) beats SA(ffn) by 1.7 R-2 / 0.8 BLEU (Sec. 4.3). ICLR 2022 (spotlight) confirmed.

methods.name: MAM Adapter
methods.paper_title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: \text{attention: } \mathrm{head} = \mathrm{Attn}\big(xW_q,\ [P_k; CW_k],\ [P_v; CW_v]\big),\ P_k,P_v\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d/n_h}\ (\ell=30);\quad \text{FFN: } h \leftarrow \mathrm{FFN}(x) + s\cdot W_{up}\,\sigma(W_{down}\,x),\ r=512;\ \text{backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2\ell d + 2rd\ \text{per layer at inference }(\ell = 30,\ r = 512;\ \text{prefix trained through an MLP reparameterization})
methods.locus: prefix vectors at every attention layer (small budget) plus a scaled parallel adapter at every FFN (large budget)
methods.structure: Sum of two of the unified-view instances in each layer: a softmax-gated parallel modification of attention heads (prefix tuning) and a scaled parallel bottleneck on the FFN, with the parameter budget deliberately allocated mostly to the FFN.
methods.mergeable_reason: Prefixes add attention slots and the FFN adapter is nonlinear.
methods.identity_at_init: Partial: the scaled parallel adapter starts at 0 (W_up = 0), but prefixes change attention from the first step (prefix tuning has no exact identity init).
methods.key_idea: Transfer the favourable design choices found by the unified analysis: parallel insertion, FFN modification with large capacity, scaling composition, and multi-head attention modification with a tiny prefix.
methods.results_note: With 6.7% tuned parameters, MAM matches full fine-tuning on XSum and en-ro and is the best of the compared PEFT methods; with RoBERTa-base and 0.5% parameters it reaches 87.4 MNLI / 94.2 SST-2 vs 87.6 / 94.6 for full fine-tuning.

relations.note: Scaled parallel adapter at the FFN.
Prefix tuning (l=30) at attention.

methods.verification_notes: Prefix l=30 at attention plus scaled PA r=512 at the FFN (Sec. 4.6), prefixes reparameterized by an MLP during training (App. A). 6.7% (XSum/en-ro) and 0.5% (MNLI 87.4 / SST-2 94.2) confirmed. AdapterHub MAMConfig = PrefixTuning(bottleneck 800) + ParBn(reduction 2, scaling 4).

methods.name: UniPELT
methods.full_name: UniPELT: unified, gated parameter-efficient language model tuning
methods.paper_title: UniPELT: A Unified Framework for Parameter-Efficient Language Model Tuning
methods.formula_latex: h'_A = \mathcal{G}_A\,W_{up}\,\phi(W_{down}\,h_{FN}) + h_F;\quad K' = [\mathcal{G}_P P_K;\,K],\ V' = [\mathcal{G}_P P_V;\,V];\quad W = W_0 + \mathcal{G}_L\,\Delta W_{\text{LoRA}};\quad \mathcal{G}_m = \mathrm{sigmoid}\big(\mathrm{FFN}_m(\cdot)\big)\in(0,1),\ m\in\{A,P,L\};\ \text{backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2rd\ (\text{adapter}) + 2\ell d\ (\text{prefix}) + 2\,r'(d_{in}+d_{out})\ (\text{LoRA on } W_q,W_v) + O(d)\ \text{gates, per layer}
methods.locus: sequential adapter after the FFN, prefixes at attention keys/values, LoRA on W_q and W_v, each with its own gate in every layer
methods.structure: Input-dependent sigmoid-gated sum of three heterogeneous submodules inside each layer (serial adapter, prefix, LoRA): a learned, per-example mixture over PEFT 'experts', with each gate able to switch its submodule off.
methods.mergeable_reason: Adapter and prefix branches are not mergeable and the LoRA gate depends on the input.
methods.identity_at_init: Not exact: inherits submodule initializations (LoRA B = 0 and near-zero adapters, but prefixes perturb attention from the start).
methods.key_idea: Rather than choosing one PEFT method per task, include adapter, prefix tuning and LoRA as submodules and learn gates that activate whichever combination suits the data and task.
methods.results_note: On GLUE, UniPELT gains 1-4 points over the best individual submodule in low-resource settings, often exceeds the upper bound of its submodules, and matches or beats fine-tuning with more data.

relations.note: Gated sequential bottleneck adapter submodule. The paper cites Houlsby et al. but places one adapter after the FFN (Pfeiffer-style placement, also AdapterHub UniPELTConfig = SeqBn reduction 16).
Gated prefix submodule.
Gate replaces LoRA's constant scaling.

methods.verification_notes: Gates G_A, G_P and G_L (sigmoid FFNs), G_A h_A + h_F, gated prefixes and G_L replacing LoRA's alpha all match Sec. 3. Defaults L=10, D_mid=48 and LoRA rank 8 on W_q,W_v are confirmed. ACL 2022 confirmed.
corrections: relations[houlsby-adapter].note: clarified that UniPELT uses a single post-FFN adapter (Eq. 1 uses h_FN).

methods.name: AdaMix
methods.paper_title: AdaMix: Mixture-of-Adaptations for Parameter-efficient Model Tuning
methods.formula_latex: \text{train: } x \leftarrow x + f\big(x\,\mathcal{W}^{down}_{i,k}\big)\,\mathcal{W}^{up}_{i,j},\ \ (j,k)\ \text{sampled uniformly per step};\ \ \mathcal{L} = \mathrm{CE} + \tfrac12\big(\mathrm{KL}(z^{\mathcal{A}}\Vert z^{\mathcal{B}}) + \mathrm{KL}(z^{\mathcal{B}}\Vert z^{\mathcal{A}})\big);\quad \text{inference: } \mathcal{W}'^{up}_{i} = \tfrac1M\sum_{j}\mathcal{W}^{up}_{ij},\ \mathcal{W}'^{down}_{i} = \tfrac1M\sum_{j}\mathcal{W}^{down}_{ij}
methods.trainable_params: (M+1)\,rd\ (+\text{biases})\ \text{per adapter during training in the default setting (} M \text{ down-projections, one shared up-projection, Sec. 3.4)},\ 2Mrd \text{ without sharing};\ 2rd\ \text{per adapter after merging (default } M=4)
methods.locus: Houlsby adapter positions (or LoRA matrices when the underlying method is LoRA)
methods.structure: A sparse mixture of M adapter 'experts' per layer with random (parameter-free) routing during training, consistency-regularized between two stochastic routes, and collapsed by weight averaging into a single adapter of the original size for inference (a model-soup within one layer).
methods.mergeable_reason: The averaged adapter is still a nonlinear bottleneck (mergeable into W only when the underlying method is LoRA).
methods.identity_at_init: Inherits the underlying PEFT initialization (approximate identity for adapters; exact for LoRA with B = 0).
methods.key_idea: Train several adaptation modules per layer with stochastic routing (same FLOPs as one), then average them into one module, gaining ensemble-like benefits at the cost and size of a single adapter.
methods.results_note: Tuning 0.1-0.2% of parameters, AdaMix outperforms full fine-tuning on all GLUE tasks with RoBERTa-large (0.23%) and beats LoRA and adapters on E2E NLG with GPT-2.

relations.note: Mixture of Houlsby adapters.
Also instantiated as a mixture of LoRA modules.
Mixes adapters without input-dependent routing at inference.

methods.verification_notes: Stochastic routing x <- x + f(x W^down_ik) W^up_ij, symmetric-KL consistency loss, inference-time weight averaging and M=4 match Sec. 3. '0.1-0.2%' and '0.23%' (RoBERTa-large GLUE table) are both stated in the paper. EMNLP 2022 confirmed.
corrections: trainable_params: 'M*2rd (up-projections may be shared)' -> '(M+1)rd'. The paper's default shares the up-projection (W^up_ij = W^up_i), giving M down- plus 1 up-projection.

methods.name: LLaMA-Adapter
methods.full_name: LLaMA-Adapter (adaption prompts with zero-initialized gated attention)
methods.paper_title: LLaMA-Adapter: Efficient Fine-tuning of Language Models with Zero-init Attention
methods.formula_latex: S_l = \tfrac{Q_lK_l^{\top}}{\sqrt{d}},\ \ K_l = [P_l;T_l;t_l]W_k,\ V_l = [P_l;T_l;t_l]W_v;\quad S^{g}_l = \big[\mathrm{softmax}(S^{K}_l)\cdot\tanh(g_l);\ \mathrm{softmax}(S^{M+1}_l)\big];\quad t^{o}_l = W_o\,S^{g}_l V_l;\ \ P_l\in\mathbb{R}^{\ell\times d}\ \text{and per-head gates } g_l\ \text{trained (top } L' \text{ layers)};\ W_{q,k,v,o}\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: L'\ell d + L' n_h\ \ (\ell = 10,\ L' = 30 \Rightarrow \approx 1.2\text{M for LLaMA-7B})
methods.locus: self-attention of the topmost L' layers: learnable adaption prompts used as extra keys/values (through the frozen W_k, W_v) with a gated, separately normalized softmax
methods.structure: Learned prompt tokens prepended at each upper layer and attended through their own softmax whose output is multiplied by a zero-initialized tanh gate; because the word-token softmax is kept separate, the layer equals the original attention plus an additive gated prefix branch. In He et al.'s unified view this is a zero-gated parallel attention branch, whose softmax bottleneck has width \ell and whose projections are tied to the frozen W_{q,k,v,o}.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adaption prompts add attention slots in the top layers at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: g_l = 0 gives tanh(g_l) = 0, so the prompt branch contributes nothing and the separately normalized word-token attention is unchanged.
methods.key_idea: Prefix-like prompts in the upper layers combined with a zero-initialized gate inject instruction-following ability progressively without disturbing the pretrained model at the start of training; the same zero-init attention also injects image tokens for multimodal reasoning.
methods.results_note: Fine-tunes frozen LLaMA-7B on 52K self-instruct demonstrations with 1.2M parameters in under one hour on 8 A100s, giving instruction-following comparable to fully fine-tuned Alpaca-7B; also extends to ScienceQA and other multimodal benchmarks.

relations.note: Prompts in upper layers, routed through frozen K/V projections and zero-gated.

methods.verification_notes: S^g = [softmax(S^K) tanh(g); softmax(S^{M+1})], per-head zero-init gates, K=10 prompts in the top L=30 of 32 layers and 1.2M parameters all match Sec. 3. ICLR 2024 confirmed. HF PEFT AdaptionPromptConfig(adapter_len, adapter_layers) exists in v0.21.1 (llama, mistral, gpt2). HF uses one scalar zero-init gate per layer applied without tanh, not per-head tanh gates.
corrections: Removed relation 'dual-to parallel-adapter'. It is not a duality, and 'special-case-of' would overstate it (RoPE-rotated queries, tied projections). The unified-view reading is kept as a sentence in structure.

methods.name: LLaMA-Adapter V2
methods.full_name: LLaMA-Adapter V2: parameter-efficient visual instruction model
methods.paper_title: LLaMA-Adapter V2: Parameter-Efficient Visual Instruction Model
methods.formula_latex: y = W_0x \;\to\; y = s\cdot(W_0x + b),\ \ b\ \text{init } 0,\ s\ \text{init } 1\ \text{(every linear layer; released code applies } s \text{ to the input: } y = W_0(s\odot x) + b);\ \ +\ \text{zero-gated adaption prompts in the last } L' \text{ layers and visual tokens with zero-init attention in early layers; norms unfrozen; } W_0 \text{ frozen}
methods.trainable_params: (d_{in}+d_{out})\ \text{per linear layer (scale + bias)} + \text{norm gains} + L'\ell d + \text{gates} + \text{early visual prompts/projection}\ \ (\text{paper: bias/scale/norm part} \approx 5\text{M} = 0.04\%;\ \approx 14\text{M new parameters over LLaMA in total})
methods.locus: every linear layer (bias + scale), all normalization layers, adaption prompts in the last layers, visual prompts in early layers
methods.structure: Composite of (i) affine reparameterization of every linear map by a diagonal scale and bias (a BitFit/SSF-like action, mergeable), (ii) LLaMA-Adapter zero-gated prefix attention in the upper layers, and (iii) early fusion of visual tokens, with disjoint parameter groups trained on image-text vs instruction data.
methods.mergeable_reason: The scale/bias part can be folded into W_0, but the gated adaption prompts and visual-token attention cannot.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: bias 0, scale 1 and zero-initialized attention gates leave the model unchanged at init.
methods.key_idea: Unlock more capacity cheaply (bias + scale on all linear layers, unfrozen norms), inject visual tokens early and instruction prompts late, and train the two parameter groups on disjoint data to avoid interference between image-text alignment and instruction following; expert captioning/OCR models can be plugged in at inference.
methods.results_note: Adds about 0.04% (~5M) new parameters to LLaMA for language instruction tuning and obtains open-ended multimodal instruction following trained only on image-text pairs plus language instruction data.

relations.note: Adds bias/scale tuning, early visual fusion and disjoint-parameter joint training.
Bias tuning of linear layers (plus scale).

methods.verification_notes: Eq. 1 y = s(Wx+b), b=0, s=1 confirmed. Released chat65b code applies s elementwise to the input and b to the output (forward_linear_with_scale_and_bias), i.e. W(s.x)+b, so per-layer cost is d_in+d_out. No peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar: arXiv only).
corrections: trainable_params: '~14M tuned in total for the 7B multimodal model' -> the paper's own statements (~5M = 0.04% for bias/scale/norm; ~14M new parameters over LLaMA). The paper does not tie 14M to the 7B multimodal variant only.
confidence: 'medium' -> 'high'. Every field was checked against the paper, the official code and (for ShadowPEFT) the HF PEFT source.

methods.name: Side-Tuning
methods.paper_title: Side-Tuning: A Baseline for Network Adaptation via Additive Side Networks
methods.formula_latex: R(x) = \alpha\,B(x) + (1-\alpha)\,S(x),\quad B\ \text{frozen base},\ S\ \text{trainable side network},\ \alpha\ \text{learned or scheduled (e.g. } \alpha(N) = \tfrac{k}{k+N})
methods.trainable_params: |\theta_S| + 1\ \ (\text{side network of any size: a copy of } B, \text{ a distilled small net, or a tiny MLP})
methods.locus: representation level: late fusion of base and side features before the task decoder
methods.structure: Late-fusion side network: an alpha-blend (convex combination) of frozen base features and side-network features computed from the same input, with no access to intermediate backbone activations; alpha = 1 is feature extraction, alpha = 0 with S a copy of B is fine-tuning.
methods.mergeable_reason: The side network is a separate forward computation that must run at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact when S is initialized as a copy of B (the paper's default when architectures match): R(x) = B(x) for any alpha; otherwise S is initialized by distillation from B (approximate).
methods.key_idea: Adapt a frozen network by learning a residual side network whose output is blended with the base representation; it never degrades the base task and treats the base as a black box (it can even be a non-network).
methods.results_note: Competitive with fine-tuning on transfer and incremental-learning benchmarks (iCIFAR, iTaskonomy, Habitat RL, SQuAD v2 with BERT) without forgetting, often with side networks much smaller than the base.

relations.note: LST extends side networks with ladder connections to intermediate activations for memory efficiency.

methods.verification_notes: Alpha-blending R = alpha B + (1-alpha) S, curriculum alpha(N)=k/(k+N), side net initialized as a copy of the base or by distillation: all match Sec. 3. ECCV 2020 confirmed via Crossref (LNCS).

methods.name: LST
methods.paper_title: LST: Ladder Side-Tuning for Parameter and Memory Efficient Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: h^{g}_{i} = \mathrm{Layer}^{g}_{i}\big(\mu_i\,\mathrm{Down}_i(h^{f}_{i}) + (1-\mu_i)\,h^{g}_{i-1}\big),\ \ \mu_i = \mathrm{sigmoid}(\alpha_i/T),\ \alpha_i\ \text{init } 0,\ T=0.1;\quad \hat y = \mathrm{LMHead}\big(\mathrm{Up}(h^{g}_{N})\big);\ \ \text{backbone } f \text{ frozen and run forward-only; side network } g,\ \mathrm{Down}_i,\ \mathrm{Up}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: \approx |\theta_f|/r^{2} + O(L\,d^{2}/r)\ \ (\text{side Transformer with all widths divided by the reduction factor } r,\ \text{plus ladder projections})
methods.locus: a separate thin side network fed by shortcut ('ladder') connections from every backbone layer (and the embeddings); predictions come from the side network through the frozen LM head
methods.structure: Side network = 1/r-width pruned copy of the backbone receiving, at each depth, a gated convex combination of a linearly down-projected backbone activation and its own previous state; information flows only backbone -> side, so no gradient enters the backbone.
methods.mergeable_reason: The side network is extra computation at inference (it produces the prediction).
methods.identity_at_init: No: the output is produced by the side network, so the model does not equal the backbone at init; instead the side network is initialized by structural pruning of backbone weights (Fisher-information row importance) and gates start at mu = 0.5.
methods.key_idea: Parameter efficiency is not memory efficiency: by never backpropagating through the backbone (gradients only flow through a small ladder-connected side network), training memory drops far below adapters or LoRA.
methods.results_note: On GLUE with T5-base, LST saves 69% of full fine-tuning memory (2.7x more savings than Adapter/LoRA at similar parameter usage) and beats Adapter and LoRA in the low-memory regime; it also scales to T5-3B and CLIP-T5 vision-language tasks.

relations.note: Adds ladder connections to intermediate activations and pruning-based init.
Both read intermediate backbone states into a side network.
Compared in the memory-accuracy trade-off.

methods.verification_notes: Gate mu_i = sigmoid(alpha_i/T) with alpha_i zero-init and T=0.1, 1/r-width side net, down/up projections, reuse of the frozen embeddings and LM head, and Fisher-based structural-pruning init all match Sec. 3. 69% memory / 2.7x confirmed. NeurIPS 2022 confirmed.

methods.name: Res-Tuning
methods.full_name: Res-Tuning / Res-Tuning-Bypass: tuners unbound from the backbone
methods.paper_title: Res-Tuning: A Flexible and Efficient Tuning Paradigm via Unbinding Tuner from Backbone
methods.formula_latex: x' = \mathrm{OP}(x) + \text{Res-Tuner}(x),\ \ \mathrm{OP}\in\{\mathrm{MHA},\mathrm{FFN},\text{block}\}\ \text{frozen};\quad \text{Bypass: } x^{b}_{0} = x_0,\ \ x^{b}_{l} = \lambda\,\text{Res-Tuner}_{h}(x_l) + (1-\lambda)\,\text{Res-Tuner}_{v}(x^{b}_{l-1}),\ \lambda = \mathrm{sigmoid}(\cdot)\ \text{init } 0.5
methods.trainable_params: \sum_{\text{tuned ops}} |\theta_{\text{tuner}}|\ \ (\text{tuner-dependent, e.g. } 2rd \text{ per bottleneck tuner})
methods.locus: tuners in parallel to MHA, FFN and whole blocks (Res-Tuning), or a detached bypass network fed by every block output (Res-Tuning-Bypass)
methods.structure: 'Unbinding': prefix, prompt and adapter tuning are rewritten (with empirical equivalence) as frozen operation plus a parallel residual tuner, so tuners become free-standing modules added to backbone operations; the Bypass variant assembles horizontal (backbone -> bypass) and vertical (bypass -> bypass) tuners into a ladder-like side network.
methods.mergeable_reason: Tuners are generally nonlinear (attention or MLP) modules, and the Bypass variant is a separate network.
methods.identity_at_init: Depends on the tuner instantiation (zero-initialized output projections give the identity in the attached form); the Bypass variant does not reproduce the backbone at init.
methods.key_idea: Decoupling tuner design from the backbone structure lets any tuner be attached anywhere and combined freely, and detaching the tuners into a bypass avoids backpropagating through the backbone and allows one backbone pass for many tasks.
methods.results_note: State-of-the-art VTAB-1K accuracy among PETL methods at similar parameter counts; Res-Tuning-Bypass cuts training memory by 49.7% and multi-task inference time by 80.9% on discriminative tasks, and by 70.7% / 83.6% for Stable Diffusion generation.

relations.note: Any tuner placed in parallel to any frozen operation.
Prefix tuning unbound as a separate attention over prefixes added to MHA.
Bypass is a ladder-style side network for memory efficiency.

methods.verification_notes: x' = OP(x) + Res-Tuner(x) and the bypass x^b_l = lambda RT_h(x_l) + (1-lambda) RT_v(x^b_{l-1}), with lambda = sigmoid init 0.5, match Sec. 3. 49.7%/80.9% and 70.7%/83.6% savings confirmed. NeurIPS 2023 confirmed via arXiv comment.
corrections: code_url: '' -> ModelScope SWIFT. ResTuningConfig in swift/tuners/restuning.py implements Res-Tuning and cites the paper. There is no standalone repository; the project page links only the arXiv paper.

methods.name: ControlNet
methods.full_name: ControlNet: trainable-copy side network with zero convolutions
methods.paper_title: Adding Conditional Control to Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
methods.formula_latex: y_c = \mathcal{F}(x;\Theta) + \mathcal{Z}\big(\mathcal{F}(x + \mathcal{Z}(c;\Theta_{z1});\Theta_c);\Theta_{z2}\big),\quad \Theta\ \text{frozen},\ \Theta_c \leftarrow \Theta\ \text{(trainable copy)},\ \mathcal{Z} = 1{\times}1\ \text{conv with zero weights and bias}
methods.trainable_params: |\Theta_c| + |\Theta_{z}| + |\mathcal{E}|\ \ (\text{trainable copy of the 12 encoder blocks and the middle block of the SD U-Net, the zero convolutions, and a tiny 4-layer conv encoder } \mathcal{E} \text{ mapping the } 512^2 \text{ condition to } 64^2)
methods.locus: trainable copy of the U-Net encoder and middle block; its outputs are added through zero convolutions to the skip connections and middle block of the frozen U-Net
methods.structure: Side network = trainable copy of the encoder that additionally receives the condition c, connected to the frozen network at both ends through zero-initialized 1x1 convolutions; it extends the input object from x to (x, c) and adds residual corrections to the frozen decoder's skip features.
methods.mergeable_reason: The copy processes the extra condition input and must run at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: both zero convolutions output 0 at the first step, so y_c = F(x; Theta) and the trainable copy starts as the pretrained encoder.
methods.key_idea: Reuse the deep pretrained encoder as a backbone for learning a new conditioning signal by training a copy of it and connecting it with zero convolutions, which protects the frozen model from harmful gradients early in training.
methods.results_note: Adds spatial controls (edges, depth, segmentation, human pose, etc.) to Stable Diffusion, with training robust on both small (<50k) and large (>1M) datasets.

relations.note: Copy-initialized side network added to a frozen model.
Lighter-weight alternative for spatial conditioning.

methods.verification_notes: Eq. 2 y_c = F(x;Theta) + Z(F(x + Z(c;Theta_z1);Theta_c);Theta_z2), with zero 1x1 convs and a trainable copy of the 12 encoder blocks plus the middle block, matches the paper. ICCV 2023 is the accepted venue (arXiv has no journal-ref).
corrections: trainable_params: added the tiny condition encoder E(.) (four 4x4 conv layers, Sec. 3.3), which is also trained.

methods.name: T2I-Adapter
methods.full_name: T2I-Adapter: lightweight condition adapters for text-to-image diffusion
methods.paper_title: T2I-Adapter: Learning Adapters to Dig out More Controllable Ability for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
methods.formula_latex: F_c = \mathcal{F}_{AD}(C),\quad \hat F^{\,i}_{enc} = F^{\,i}_{enc} + F^{\,i}_{c},\ i\in\{1,2,3,4\};\quad \text{multi-condition: } F_c = \sum_{k=1}^{K}\omega_k\,\mathcal{F}^{k}_{AD}(C_k);\ \ \text{SD frozen, } \mathcal{F}_{AD}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: \approx 77\text{M per adapter (18M small, 5M tiny variants)}
methods.locus: external condition encoder whose four multi-scale features are added to the frozen U-Net encoder features
methods.structure: Additive feature injection from a small external network (pixel-unshuffle, convolutions and residual blocks): each condition defines a translation of the frozen encoder's intermediate states at four scales, and several adapters compose by weighted sum without retraining.
methods.mergeable_reason: The adapter processes the extra condition input at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Not guaranteed by construction (no zero-init is described); the original model is recovered exactly when no adapter is attached or its weight omega_k = 0.
methods.key_idea: Align the internal knowledge of a frozen text-to-image model with external control signals using small, composable condition encoders that only need one pass per generation.
methods.results_note: Supports sketch, depth, segmentation, keypose and color-palette control of Stable Diffusion with ~77M parameters, and multi-condition control by composing adapters without extra training.

relations.note: Smaller external encoder instead of a trainable copy of the U-Net encoder.
Image-prompt vs structural-condition adapters for frozen diffusion models.

methods.verification_notes: Additive multi-scale encoder injection, weighted multi-adapter composition F_c = sum omega_k F_AD^k(C_k), and ~77M/18M/5M parameters match the paper. AAAI 2024 confirmed via Crossref DOI 10.1609/aaai.v38i5.28226.

methods.name: IP-Adapter
methods.full_name: IP-Adapter: image prompt adapter with decoupled cross-attention
methods.paper_title: IP-Adapter: Text Compatible Image Prompt Adapter for Text-to-Image Diffusion Models
methods.formula_latex: Z^{new} = \mathrm{Attention}(Q,K,V) + \lambda\cdot\mathrm{Attention}(Q,K',V'),\quad Q = ZW_q,\ K = c_tW_k,\ V = c_tW_v\ \text{(frozen)},\ \ K' = c_iW'_k,\ V' = c_iW'_v\ \text{(trained, init from } W_k,W_v)
methods.trainable_params: 2\,d_{c}\,d\ \text{per cross-attention layer } (W'_k,W'_v) + \text{image-embedding projection}\ \ (\approx 22\text{M for SD 1.5, 16 layers})
methods.locus: a parallel image cross-attention branch added to every cross-attention layer of the U-Net, sharing the frozen query
methods.structure: Decoupled cross-attention: a second attention over new image-prompt tokens (with its own key/value projections and its own softmax) is added to the frozen text cross-attention output; lambda scales the branch. Structurally this is the same decoupled-softmax parallel attention branch as LLaMA-Adapter's gated prompts, but its keys/values come from an input (the image embedding) through new trainable projections.
methods.mergeable_reason: The image branch attends over extra tokens derived from the image prompt at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Not at init (W'_k, W'_v are copied from W_k, W_v so the branch is active from the start); the original model is recovered exactly with lambda = 0.
methods.key_idea: Instead of concatenating image and text features into the frozen cross-attention, add a separate cross-attention for image features so a small adapter gives strong image-prompt control while remaining compatible with text prompts and structural controls.
methods.results_note: A ~22M-parameter IP-Adapter is comparable to or better than fully fine-tuned image-prompt models and remains compatible with text prompts and ControlNet-style controls.

relations.note: Another lightweight conditioning adapter for frozen diffusion models.

methods.verification_notes: Decoupled cross-attention Z = Attn(Q,K,V) + lambda Attn(Q,K',V'), with W'_k, W'_v initialized from W_k, W_v, 16 cross-attention layers and ~22M parameters, matches Sec. 3. lambda=1 in training. No peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar/Crossref): arXiv.
corrections: Removed relation 'dual-to llama-adapter'. The two share a mechanism but are not dual, and neither is a special case of the other. The analogy now sits in structure.

methods.name: AdaptFormer
methods.paper_title: AdaptFormer: Adapting Vision Transformers for Scalable Visual Recognition
methods.formula_latex: \tilde x_\ell = W_{up}\,\mathrm{ReLU}\big(W_{down}\,\mathrm{LN}(x'_\ell)\big),\quad x_\ell = \mathrm{MLP}\big(\mathrm{LN}(x'_\ell)\big) + s\cdot\tilde x_\ell + x'_\ell,\ \ s = 0.1;\ \ \text{ViT frozen, } W_{down},W_{up}\ \text{trained}
methods.trainable_params: 2rd + r + d\ \text{per block}
methods.locus: in parallel to the MLP (FFN) block of every ViT layer
methods.structure: Scaled parallel bottleneck adapter on the FFN (AdaptMLP), i.e. the vision instance of the scaled parallel adapter with s < 1.
methods.mergeable_reason: Nonlinear bottleneck in parallel with a nonlinear MLP.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W_up and all adapter biases are zero-initialized (W_down Kaiming-normal), so the branch outputs 0 at init.
methods.key_idea: Adapt ViTs through a lightweight parallel branch next to the MLP rather than through token-space prompts, which scales to the many tokens of video.
methods.results_note: With ViT-B, ~1.5% extra parameters give about 10% and 19% relative improvement over full fine-tuning on Something-Something v2 and HMDB51, and it beats VPT on image benchmarks.

relations.note: Same functional form (scaled parallel adapter at the FFN), concurrently proposed for vision.
Main vision PEFT baseline.

methods.verification_notes: x_l = MLP(LN(x')) + s ReLU(LN(x') W_down) W_up + x', s=0.1, W_down Kaiming-normal, W_up and biases zero (Sec. 3, 4.1). 1.5% params with ~10%/19% relative gains on SSv2/HMDB51 confirmed. NeurIPS 2022 confirmed.

methods.name: Convpass
methods.paper_title: Convolutional Bypasses Are Better Vision Transformer Adapters
methods.formula_latex: X' \leftarrow X + \mathrm{MHSA/MLP}\big(\mathrm{LN}(X)\big) + s\cdot\mathrm{Convpass}\big(\mathrm{LN}(X)\big),\quad \mathrm{Convpass} = \mathrm{Conv}^{\uparrow}_{1\times1}\circ\mathrm{GELU}\circ\mathrm{Conv}_{3\times3}\circ\mathrm{GELU}\circ\mathrm{Conv}^{\downarrow}_{1\times1}\ \text{on tokens reshaped to the patch grid ([cls] as a } 1{\times}1 \text{ image)}
methods.trainable_params: 2L\big((2r+1)d + 9r^2 + 2r\big)\ \text{in total (two Convpass per layer; paper } r = 8)
methods.locus: in parallel to both MHSA and MLP in every ViT block
methods.structure: Parallel convolutional bottleneck (ResNet-style 1x1-3x3-1x1 block on the reshaped token grid) that injects spatial-locality inductive bias; unrolled, each layer becomes an ensemble of transformer, CNN and hybrid paths.
methods.mergeable_reason: The 3x3 convolution mixes neighbouring tokens and the block is nonlinear, so it cannot be absorbed into per-token frozen weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact in the official code: up-projection weights and biases are zero-initialized (down-projection Xavier; 3x3 conv initialized to identity at its centre tap).
methods.key_idea: Language-oriented adapters lack visual inductive bias; a convolutional bypass restores 2D locality during fine-tuning and works especially well in the low-data regime.
methods.results_note: With under 0.5% extra parameters, Convpass outperforms language-oriented PETL modules (Adapter, LoRA, VPT, NOAH) on VTAB-1K and few-shot fine-grained classification.

relations.note: Parallel insertion with a scaling factor, with a convolutional bottleneck.
Vision adapter baseline.

methods.verification_notes: ECAI 2024 confirmed via Crossref (FAIA vol., DOI 10.3233/FAIA240489). The parameter count 2L((2h+1)d+9h^2+2h) with h=8 is stated in Sec. 4. Official code: up-projection weights and biases zero, down Xavier, 3x3 conv zero plus identity at the centre tap (unless xavier_init=True).
corrections: authors: 'Jie et al.' -> 'Jie and Deng'. The paper has two authors (Shibo Jie, Zhi-Hong Deng), and the catalog uses 'A and B' for two-author papers, as in 'Steitz and Roth'.

methods.name: ST-Adapter
methods.paper_title: ST-Adapter: Parameter-Efficient Image-to-Video Transfer Learning
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{ST\text{-}Adapter}(X) = X + f\big(\mathrm{DWConv3D}(XW_{down})\big)\,W_{up},\quad X\in\mathbb{R}^{T\times N\times d}\ \text{reshaped to } T\times h\times w\times r \text{ before the depth-wise } 3{\times}1{\times}1 \text{ convolution};\ \text{image backbone frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2rd + k_Tk_Hk_W\,r + O(d + r)\ \text{per adapter } (k = 3{\times}1{\times}1)
methods.locus: one adapter before the MHSA of every ViT block (operating on the T frames' patch tokens)
methods.structure: Serial residual bottleneck with a depth-wise spatio-temporal convolution in the compressed space, i.e. a token-mixing linear operator across neighbouring frames inserted between down- and up-projection; it gives an image model temporal reasoning. (The official code has no activation between the depth-wise convolution and W_up, and adapts only the patch tokens, leaving [CLS] unchanged.)
methods.mergeable_reason: The 3D convolution mixes tokens across frames and positions, so it cannot be folded into per-token frozen weights.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact in the official code: depth-wise 3D-conv weights and all biases are zero-initialized, so the adapter outputs X at init.
methods.key_idea: Turn a frozen image transformer into a video model by inserting cheap adapters whose bottleneck contains a depth-wise 3D convolution for temporal modelling.
methods.results_note: With CLIP ViT-B/16, ST-Adapter matches full fine-tuning on Kinetics-400 (82.0 vs 81.7) and SSv2 (66.3 vs 66.1) while updating 7.2M vs 121.6M parameters.

relations.note: Adds a spatio-temporal operator inside the bottleneck.
Image-to-video adaptation by adapters.

methods.verification_notes: Eq. 2 matches the paper. The default kernel is 3x1x1 (Table 7), one adapter before MHSA, bottleneck 384 in the main setting. Official code zero-inits the conv weight/bias and both linear biases. K400 82.0 vs 81.7, SSv2 66.3 vs 66.1, 7.2M vs 121.57M confirmed. NeurIPS 2022 confirmed.
corrections: structure: noted that the official models_adapter.py applies fc1 -> depthwise Conv3d -> fc2 with no activation f and skips the [CLS] token, unlike the paper's Eq. 2.

methods.name: AIM
methods.full_name: Adapting Image Models (spatial, temporal and joint adaptation)
methods.paper_title: AIM: Adapting Image Models for Efficient Video Action Recognition
methods.formula_latex: z^{T}_{l} = z_{l-1} + \mathrm{Ad}_T\big(\text{T-MSA}(\mathrm{LN}(z_{l-1}))\big),\ \ z^{S}_{l} = z^{T}_{l} + \mathrm{Ad}_S\big(\text{S-MSA}(\mathrm{LN}(z^{T}_{l}))\big),\ \ z_l = z^{S}_{l} + \mathrm{MLP}\big(\mathrm{LN}(z^{S}_{l})\big) + s\cdot\mathrm{Ad}_J\big(\mathrm{LN}(z^{S}_{l})\big);\ \ \text{T-MSA} = \text{S-MSA frozen, applied along time};\ s = 0.5
methods.trainable_params: 3\,(2rd + r + d)\ \text{per block } (r = d/4)
methods.locus: three adapters per ViT block: after the reused temporal attention (no skip), after spatial attention (with skip), and parallel to the MLP (no skip, scaled by s)
methods.structure: Reuses the frozen spatial self-attention as a temporal attention by re-indexing tokens (the same frozen operator acting along a different axis), and adds serial adapters after both attentions plus a scaled parallel adapter at the MLP.
methods.mergeable_reason: Nonlinear adapters and an additional (reused) attention pass at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact. The second FC layer of every adapter is zero-initialized, and the temporal and joint (MLP-parallel) adapters have no internal skip connection, so both branches output 0 while the spatial adapter (with skip) is the identity. The model equals the image model at init.
methods.key_idea: Equip a frozen image transformer with spatio-temporal reasoning without new attention weights: reuse its attention over time and train only lightweight adapters.
methods.results_note: Achieves comparable or better accuracy than fully fine-tuned video models with far fewer tunable parameters on four action-recognition benchmarks (Kinetics-400/700, Something-Something v2, Diving-48).

relations.note: Image-to-video adaptation with adapters.
Joint adaptation is a scaled parallel adapter at the MLP.

methods.verification_notes: Equations for temporal/spatial/joint adaptation, the frozen MSA reused along time, bottleneck ratio 0.25, s=0.5 and the zero-init second FC match the paper (Sec. 3, App. A) and the official code. ICLR 2023 confirmed.
corrections: identity_at_init/locus: the joint MLP-parallel adapter also has no skip (official vit_clip.py: MLP_Adapter = Adapter(skip_connect=False)). Without this, s*Adapter(LN(z)) would not vanish at init.

methods.name: RepAdapter
methods.paper_title: Towards Efficient Visual Adaption via Structural Re-parameterization
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{Ad}(x) = x + s\big(W_u(W_dx + b_d) + b_u\big),\ \ W_d\in\mathbb{R}^{r\times d}\ \text{dense},\ W_u\in\mathbb{R}^{d\times r}\ \text{group-wise (block-diagonal, } k \text{ groups)};\quad \text{placed before a frozen projection } W_0:\ W_0' = W_0\,(I + sW_uW_d),\ \ b_0' = b_0 + sW_0(W_ub_d + b_u)
methods.trainable_params: rd + \tfrac{rd}{k} + r + d\ \text{per adapter (two adapters per block)}
methods.locus: sequentially before MHA (i.e. feeding W_q, W_k, W_v) and before the FFN (feeding W_1) in every ViT block, after LayerNorm
methods.structure: Activation-free serial adapter I + sW_uW_d (identity plus a rank-\le r, group-structured matrix) placed immediately before a frozen linear map, so it is absorbed by right multiplication W_0 \mapsto W_0(I + sW_uW_d); equivalently an additive update \Delta W = sW_0W_uW_d. Structurally it is a low-rank, token-space instance of Rebuffi et al.'s linear residual adapter I+\alpha, although RepAdapter does not cite that work. One adapter feeds W_q, W_k and W_v together, so their merged updates share the same factor.
methods.mergeable_reason: Without nonlinearity the adapter is an affine map preceding a frozen linear projection, so it folds exactly into that projection's weight and bias, giving zero extra inference cost.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact: W_u and both biases are zero-initialized (W_d Xavier), so the adapter is the identity at init.
methods.key_idea: Removing the nonlinearity of visual adapters costs no accuracy, and a linear adapter placed before a projection can be re-parameterized into it, giving adapter-style training with LoRA-like zero inference overhead.
methods.results_note: Outperforms prior PETL methods on VTAB-1k on average with zero added inference latency, and transfers to ConvNeXt, Swin, CLIP, segmentation and video tasks.

relations.note: Both have zero inference overhead after merging, and RepAdapter reports +1.6% average VTAB-1k over LoRA. RepAdapter's merged update Delta W = sW_0W_uW_d (plus a bias shift) is rank <= r, but B = sW_0W_u is tied to W_0, W_u is group-wise, and A = W_d is shared by all projections fed by the same adapter. It is a constrained LoRA-type update, not an equivalent one.
Serial bottleneck without the nonlinearity.

methods.verification_notes: Eq. 9-11 (activation-free adapter, W_ada = W_dW_u + I, Rep = W_ada W_0) and the default c=8, k=2, s searched in {0.1,...,10} match the paper. Official repadapter.py: Xavier W_d, zero W_u and biases, scale s. No peer-reviewed venue found (Semantic Scholar: arXiv only).
corrections: formula_latex: clarified that only the up-projection W_u is group-wise and the down-projection W_d is dense (paper Sec. 3.2.2 'dense-to-sparse'; code conv_A groups=1, conv_B groups=k). The old text read as if both were group-wise.
Removed relation 'builds-on residual-adapter'. RepAdapter does not cite Rebuffi et al., so the lineage claim is unsupported; the structural link was moved to structure.

relation to lora: 'equivalent-to' -> 'competes-with'. The merged update has a W_0-tied, group-structured B shared across Q/K/V plus a bias shift, so it is not equivalent to independent LoRA. The paper compares against LoRA directly.

methods.name: Mona
methods.paper_title: 5%>100%: Breaking Performance Shackles of Full Fine-Tuning on Visual Recognition Tasks
methods.formula_latex: x_{norm} = s_1\cdot\mathrm{LN}(x_0) + s_2\cdot x_0;\ \ f_{dw}(z) = z + \tfrac13\sum_{i=1}^{3}\omega^{i}_{dw}\,\hat\otimes\,z\ (3{\times}3,5{\times}5,7{\times}7);\ \ f_{pw}(z) = z + \omega_{pw}\,\bar\otimes\,z;\ \ x = x_0 + U^{l}\,\sigma\big(f_{pw}(f_{dw}(D^{l}x_{norm}))\big)
methods.trainable_params: (2r+3)d + r^2 + 84r + 2\ \text{per Mona module; two per block } (r = 64)
methods.locus: two serial Mona modules per Swin block, after the MSA and after the MLP
methods.structure: Serial residual bottleneck whose input is a learned blend of normalized and raw features and whose compressed space is processed by averaged multi-scale depth-wise convolutions and a 1x1 convolution, each with its own skip connection.
methods.mergeable_reason: Nonlinear, token-mixing convolutional bottleneck.
methods.identity_at_init: No. The paper states no identity-at-init guarantee, and the official code leaves the up-projection U^l at PyTorch's default (Kaiming-uniform) init, so the adapter output is not zero at init. In code s_1 and s_2 are per-channel vectors initialized to 1e-6 and 1.
methods.key_idea: Make visual adapters 'see' like vision models (multi-scale depth-wise filters) and let them re-normalize the frozen features, so adapter tuning can surpass full fine-tuning on dense prediction tasks. First released in Nov 2023 as arXiv:2311.15010 ('Adapter is All You Need for Tuning Visual Tasks').
methods.results_note: With Swin backbones, Mona surpasses full fine-tuning on COCO instance segmentation (about +1%), ADE20K, Pascal VOC, DOTA/STAR oriented detection and image classification.

relations.note: Serial bottleneck with visual filters and scaled LayerNorm.
Convolutional visual adapters.

methods.verification_notes: Eqs. 2-5 (x_norm = s_1|x_0|_LN + s_2 x_0, averaged 3/5/7 depth-wise convs with skip, 1x1 conv with skip, GeLU, up-projection) and the paper's per-block count 2((2n+3)m+n^2+84n+2) with n=64 are confirmed. The paper counts s_1, s_2 as 2 scalars, while the code uses d-dimensional vectors. CVPR 2025 confirmed via Crossref DOI 10.1109/CVPR52734.2025.01869.
corrections: year: 2023 -> 2024, the first-version year of the listed arXiv:2408.08345 (CVPR 2025 version). The earlier Nov 2023 preprint arXiv:2311.15010 has a different title and is mentioned in key_idea.
identity_at_init: replaced 'near-identity when the up-projection is small' with what the official code does: project2 uses the default init (not zero or small), gamma (s_1) = 1e-6, gammax (s_2) = 1.

methods.name: CLIP-Adapter
methods.full_name: CLIP-Adapter: residual feature adapters for CLIP
methods.paper_title: CLIP-Adapter: Better Vision-Language Models with Feature Adapters
methods.formula_latex: A_v(f) = \mathrm{ReLU}(f^{\top}W^{v}_{1})W^{v}_{2},\quad f^{\star} = \alpha\,A_v(f)^{\top} + (1-\alpha)\,f;\ \ (\text{optionally } W^{\star} = \beta A_t(W)^{\top} + (1-\beta)W);\quad \text{logits} \propto W^{\star}f^{\star};\ \text{CLIP encoders frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2dr\ \text{per adapted branch } (r = d/4;\ \text{default: visual branch only})
methods.locus: on the final CLIP image embedding (and optionally the text-generated classifier weights), outside the encoders
methods.structure: Residual-blended bottleneck MLP on the output embedding: a convex combination with residual ratio alpha of the frozen feature and its adapted image, i.e. post-composition of the encoder with an endomorphism of the embedding space.
methods.mergeable_reason: A nonlinear MLP after the encoder (negligible cost, but not foldable).
methods.identity_at_init: No exact identity: the bottleneck is randomly initialized; closeness to zero-shot CLIP is controlled by the residual ratio alpha (small for generic datasets, larger for fine-grained or shifted domains).
methods.key_idea: For few-shot CLIP transfer, a tiny residual feature adapter at the end of the encoder, blended with the original feature, beats learning prompts (CoOp) while avoiding overfitting.
methods.results_note: Outperforms zero-shot CLIP, linear-probe CLIP and CoOp on 11 few-shot classification datasets across shot settings, with large gains on fine-grained datasets.

relations.note: Feature adapter vs learned text prompts for few-shot CLIP.
Bottleneck adapter applied once to the output feature with a residual ratio.

methods.verification_notes: Eqs. 4-7 match the paper: A_v(f) = ReLU(f^T W1) W2 and f* = alpha A_v(f)^T + (1-alpha) f, bottleneck 256 = d/4, visual branch only by default. Official code is bias-free and adds a second ReLU after the up-projection. IJCV confirmed (online Sep 2023, print vol. 132, Feb 2024; DOI 10.1007/s11263-023-01891-x).

methods.name: Tip-Adapter
methods.paper_title: Tip-Adapter: Training-free Adaption of CLIP for Few-shot Classification
methods.formula_latex: \mathrm{logits} = \alpha\,\varphi\big(f_{test}F_{train}^{\top}\big)L_{train} + f_{test}W_c^{\top},\quad \varphi(x) = \exp\big(-\beta(1-x)\big);\quad F_{train}\in\mathbb{R}^{NK\times d}\ \text{(cached CLIP features)},\ L_{train}\in\{0,1\}^{NK\times N};\ \text{Tip-Adapter-F trains } F_{train}\ \text{only}
methods.trainable_params: 0\ (\text{Tip-Adapter});\ \ NK\,d\ (\text{Tip-Adapter-F: cache keys})
methods.locus: on the final CLIP image embedding: a key-value cache built from the K-shot N-class training set, blended with CLIP's zero-shot logits
methods.structure: Non-parametric key-value cache acting as a two-layer adapter whose first layer is the matrix of cached features (with exponential activation) and whose second layer is the one-hot label matrix, added residually to the zero-shot classifier; Tip-Adapter-F unfreezes the keys as an initialization.
methods.mergeable_reason: The cache (NK keys) must be stored and queried at inference.
methods.identity_at_init: With alpha = 0 the model is zero-shot CLIP exactly; the cache is constructed (not randomly initialized) from few-shot features, so no training is needed.
methods.key_idea: Set the adapter's weights directly from the few-shot data (keys = image features, values = labels), making CLIP adaptation training-free; optionally fine-tune the keys for a few epochs.
methods.results_note: Training-free Tip-Adapter is comparable to CoOp and CLIP-Adapter, and Tip-Adapter-F sets the state of the art on 16-shot ImageNet with only 20 epochs (vs 200 for CoOp/CLIP-Adapter), across 11 datasets. First released Nov 2021 as arXiv:2111.03930.

relations.note: A CLIP-Adapter whose bottleneck weights are set from the cache (features and one-hot labels) with an exponential activation.
Few-shot CLIP adaptation baseline.

methods.verification_notes: Eq. logits = alpha phi(f F^T) L + f W_c^T with phi(x) = exp(-beta(1-x)), and Tip-Adapter-F unfreezing only the keys F_train, match Sec. 3. ECCV 2022 confirmed via Crossref (LNCS, DOI 10.1007/978-3-031-19833-5_29).
corrections: year: 2021 -> 2022, the first-version year of the listed arXiv:2207.09519 (ECCV 2022 version). The Nov 2021 preprint arXiv:2111.03930 ('...Training-free CLIP-Adapter for Better Vision-Language Modeling') is mentioned in results_note.

methods.name: Adapter+
methods.paper_title: Adapters Strike Back
methods.formula_latex: y = \mathrm{FFN}(x) + x;\quad y \leftarrow y + s\odot\big(W_{up}\,\mathrm{GELU}(W_{down}\,y + b_{down}) + b_{up}\big),\quad s\in\mathbb{R}^{d}\ \text{learned channel-wise scaling};\ \ \text{ViT frozen}
methods.trainable_params: 2rd + r + 2d\ \text{per ViT block}
methods.locus: Post-Adapter position: once per ViT block, after the FFN including its residual add
methods.structure: Serial residual bottleneck at the end of each block whose correction is post-composed with a learned diagonal map diag(s) (channel-wise scaling); systematic study of positions (pre, post, parallel, intermediate), initializations and normalization.
methods.mergeable_reason: Nonlinear serial bottleneck.
methods.identity_at_init: Near-identity: Houlsby initialization (weights from a zero-mean Gaussian with std 0.01 truncated at 2 std, zero biases), which beat BERT and LoRA-style inits in the paper's ablation.
methods.key_idea: Plain adapters were under-reported for ViTs; placed after the block (Post-Adapter), Houlsby-initialized, without LayerNorm and with a learned channel-wise scale, they give the best parameter-accuracy trade-off.
methods.results_note: Reaches 77.6% average accuracy on VTAB (ViT-B/16) without per-task hyperparameter optimization and 90.7% on FGVC, the best parameter-accuracy trade-off among the compared methods.

relations.note: Uses the post-FFN position found by Pfeiffer et al.
Houlsby initialization.
Re-evaluated against VPT, SSF, LoRA, FacT, SPT.

methods.verification_notes: Post-Adapter x -> Adapter(FFN(x)+x) + (FFN(x)+x) with Adapter = s . (sigma(xW_down+b)W_up+b), channel-wise s in R^d, no LN, and Houlsby init (std 0.01 truncated at 2 std) match Sec. 3. VTAB 77.6% and FGVC 90.7% confirmed. CVPR 2024 confirmed via arXiv comment. AdapterHub AdapterPlusConfig (houlsby init, channel scaling) exists.

methods.name: ShadowPEFT
methods.full_name: ShadowPEFT: shadow network for parameter-efficient fine-tuning
methods.paper_title: ShadowPEFT: Shadow Network for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning
methods.formula_latex: s^{(0)} = f_{\text{shadow}}(x);\ \ \delta^{(\ell)} = h^{(\ell-1)}_{out} - s^{(\ell-1)},\ \ h^{(\ell)} = h^{(\ell-1)}_{out} + \alpha\,W^{(\ell)}_{up}W^{(\ell)}_{down}\,\delta^{(\ell)},\ \ h^{(\ell)}_{out} = f^{(\ell)}_{\text{base}}(h^{(\ell)});\ \ s^{(\ell)} = (1-g^{(\ell)})\odot s^{(\ell-1)} + g^{(\ell)}\odot T^{(\ell)}(h^{(\ell)}_{out}),\ g^{(\ell)} = \sigma\big(G^{(\ell)}(h^{(\ell)}_{out})\big);\ \ f_{\text{base}}\ \text{frozen}
methods.trainable_params: |\theta_{\text{shadow}}| + \sum_{\ell}\big(2rd + 4d\,h_g\big) + |\text{shadow head}|\ \ (W_{down},W_{up}\ \text{bias-free};\ T^{(\ell)}, G^{(\ell)}\ \text{are bias-free two-layer MLPs of width } h_g;\ \text{HF default } h_g = r = 8,\ \text{one-layer mirror shadow backbone})
methods.locus: input of every targeted decoder block (shadow injection) plus a small parallel shadow backbone whose state is carried through depth
methods.structure: Two-way coupled side network: a persistent shadow state evolves through depth by GRU-like gated convex updates from the backbone outputs, and injects a low-rank (bottleneck) correction of the discrepancy h - s into each frozen block's input; adaptation is an input-dependent trajectory rather than a static weight delta.
methods.mergeable_reason: The correction depends on an evolving, input-dependent shadow state; HF PEFT raises an error on merge for this reason.
methods.identity_at_init: Exact for the base pathway: W_up is zero-initialized, so the injected correction is 0 and the frozen model's function is unchanged at init.
methods.key_idea: Concentrate all trainable adaptation in a compact shadow model coupled layer-wise to the frozen LLM; because the shadow is trained as a full predictor it can be detached for shadow-only (e.g. edge) inference and initialized from a smaller pretrained model.
methods.results_note: On Qwen backbones at three scales, ShadowPEFT is competitive with or better than LoRA and DoRA at closely matched trainable-parameter budgets on generation and understanding benchmarks.

relations.note: Side network fed by backbone states, but with shadow-to-base injection (two-way coupling) and no aim of avoiding backbone backprop.
Main baseline; LoRA/DoRA at matched budgets.

methods.verification_notes: Eqs. 1-6 (s^(0) = f_shadow(x), delta = h_out - s, Dropout(delta W_down) W_up, h = h_out + alpha delta~, GRU-like gated update) match the paper. W_up = 0 at init. HF PEFT v0.21.1 has tuners/shadow, ShadowLayer.merge raises NotImplementedError, and the docs page package_reference/shadow exists. No venue: arXiv (v2 Sep 2026).
corrections: trainable_params: made |T|+|G| explicit as 4 d h_g (bias-free two-layer SiLU MLPs, paper App. B) and added the HF defaults.
hf_peft_config: 'ShadowConfig' -> 'ShadowConfig(r, shadow_alpha, shadow_model)' (defaults r=8, shadow_alpha=0.1, shadow_model='mirror'), matching the field style used for AdaptionPromptConfig.
confidence: 'medium' -> 'high'. Every field was checked against the paper, the official code and (for ShadowPEFT) the HF PEFT source.

papers.title: Towards a Unified View of Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning
papers.claim: Adapters, prefix tuning and LoRA are all modifications \Delta h added to specific hidden states and differ only along four axes: functional form, insertion form (sequential vs parallel), modified representation (attention vs FFN) and composition function (simple, gated, scaled); prefix tuning is exactly a softmax-gated parallel adapter on attention heads.
papers.relevance: Provides the canonical coordinate system for the adapter family (serial vs parallel composition, gating and scaling as composition laws), directly suggesting a categorical reading where adapters are endomorphisms post-composed with sublayers and parallel adapters are sums of morphisms with a common domain.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2110.04366 (He, 2021). ICLR 2022 spotlight per arXiv comment. The four design dimensions and the prefix = gated parallel adapter derivation (Sec. 3) are confirmed.

papers.title: On the Effectiveness of Adapter-based Tuning for Pretrained Language Model Adaptation
papers.claim: Adapter-based tuning yields representations that deviate less from the pretrained model than fine-tuning, mitigating forgetting; it outperforms fine-tuning on low-resource and cross-lingual tasks and is more robust to overfitting and learning-rate changes.
papers.relevance: Empirical evidence that the near-identity, frozen-backbone structure of adapters acts as an implicit regularizer toward the pretrained function, a key property for any theory of PEFT as a small deformation of a base model.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2106.03164 (Ruidan He, 2021). ACL 2021 long paper per arXiv comment. The claims match the abstract.

papers.title: AdapterHub: A Framework for Adapting Transformers
papers.claim: A framework on top of HuggingFace Transformers for training, sharing and dynamically 'stitching-in' pre-trained adapters for different tasks and languages.
papers.relevance: Made adapters first-class, swappable, composable objects (the infrastructure behind MAD-X, AdapterFusion and AdapterDrop), the practical counterpart of treating adapters as modular morphisms.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2007.07779 (Pfeiffer, 2020). EMNLP 2020 System Demonstrations per arXiv comment.

papers.title: Adapters: A Unified Library for Parameter-Efficient and Modular Transfer Learning
papers.claim: Unifies about ten adapter methods (sequential/parallel bottleneck, Compacter, prefix tuning, LoRA, (IA)^3, MAM, UniPELT, and more) behind one interface with composition blocks (Stack, Fuse, Split, BatchSplit, Parallel, Average) for building complex adapter setups.
papers.relevance: Its composition blocks are an explicit operational algebra of adapters (sequential composition, fusion, splitting, averaging), a natural target for a categorical semantics of adapter composition.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2311.11077 (Poth, 2023). EMNLP 2023 System Demonstrations per arXiv comment. '10 diverse adapter methods' and the composition blocks are confirmed.

papers.title: LLM-Adapters: An Adapter Family for Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning of Large Language Models
