papers.claim: A framework integrating series adapters, parallel adapters, prompt-based and reparameterization methods into LLaMA, BLOOM and GPT-J; the best placements are after the MLP for series adapters, parallel to the MLP for parallel adapters, and on both attention and MLP for LoRA, and 7B models with adapters can rival much larger zero-shot models on math and commonsense reasoning.
papers.relevance: Transfers the serial vs parallel adapter taxonomy to decoder-only LLMs and gives placement evidence that any structural theory of insertion sites must explain.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2304.01933 (Zhiqiang Hu, 2023). EMNLP 2023 per arXiv comment. The placement findings match Sec. 4.1 exactly.

papers.title: Modular Deep Learning
papers.claim: Surveys modular architectures in which parameter-efficient modules are conditionally routed and aggregated, giving a unified view of computation functions, routing functions and aggregation functions across many research threads.
papers.relevance: Its decomposition into modules, routing and aggregation is close to a categorical description (objects = representations, morphisms = modules, routing/aggregation = coproduct/colimit-like combinators) and covers adapters, fusion and mixtures.

papers.title: VL-Adapter: Parameter-Efficient Transfer Learning for Vision-and-Language Tasks
papers.claim: Benchmarks Adapter, HyperFormer, Compacter and prompt tuning on image-text and video-text tasks with CLIP-BART/T5 in a unified multi-task setup; a single adapter shared across tasks (4.18% of parameters for image-text, 3.39% for video-text) matches full fine-tuning.
papers.relevance: Shows that weight sharing of adapters across tasks (one module serving many tasks) is often best, informing how adapter objects should be indexed by tasks in a unified theory.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2112.06825 (Sung, 2021). CVPR 2022 per arXiv comment. 4.18% / 3.39% are confirmed in the abstract.

papers.title: Parameter-efficient fine-tuning of large-scale pre-trained language models
papers.claim: Formalizes delta tuning and divides methods into addition-based (adapters, prompts), specification-based (selective) and reparameterization-based (low-rank) families, with theoretical perspectives (optimization and optimal control) and experiments on over 100 NLP tasks.
papers.relevance: The addition-based class is the adapter family of this catalog; the three-way taxonomy is a baseline that a categorical classification should refine.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2203.06904 (Ding, 2022). Published in Nature Machine Intelligence (online 2 Mar 2023, DOI 10.1038/s42256-023-00626-4) under a different title from the arXiv one ('Delta Tuning: A Comprehensive Study of Parameter Efficient Methods for Pre-trained Language Models'). 'Over 100 NLP tasks' is confirmed.
corrections: title: removed the appended '(Delta Tuning)', which is not part of the Nature MI title. The arXiv title differs and is recorded in verification_notes.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning Design Spaces
papers.claim: Parameterizes PEFT designs by layer grouping, trainable-parameter allocation, tunable groups and strategy assignment, and finds patterns (spindle grouping, uniform allocation, tune all groups, proper strategy per group) that yield methods outperforming individual adapter, prefix, BitFit and LoRA strategies.
papers.relevance: Treats the choice of adapter type and insertion site as points in a structured design space, a precursor to treating PEFT methods as structured objects rather than isolated recipes.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2301.01821 (Jiaao Chen, 2023). ICLR 2023 per Semantic Scholar. The four components and the design patterns match the abstract.
corrections: confidence: 'medium' -> 'high'. Venue confirmed (Semantic Scholar) and the claim matches the abstract.

papers.title: Parameter-Efficient Fine-Tuning for Large Models: A Comprehensive Survey
papers.claim: Comprehensive survey of PEFT algorithms (additive incl. adapters, selective, reparameterized, hybrid), their computational overhead, applications and system design.
papers.relevance: Standard reference taxonomy for placing the adapter family (serial, parallel, hybrid adapters) alongside other PEFT families.
papers.verification_notes: arXiv 2403.14608 (Zeyu Han, 2024). TMLR 2024 per Semantic Scholar.
corrections: confidence: 'medium' -> 'high'. Venue confirmed (Semantic Scholar) and the claim matches the abstract.

notes: Scope: methods that insert new modules into the computation graph. Organised by insertion morphology: (i) serial bottleneck adapters (residual-adapter, houlsby-adapter, pfeiffer-adapter, mad-x, compacter, hyperformer, adapter-plus, st-adapter, mona, repadapter); (ii) parallel adapters (parallel-adapter, adaptformer, convpass, aim joint adapter, ip-adapter branch); (iii) side / ladder networks (side-tuning, k-adapter, ladder-side-tuning, res-tuning, controlnet, t2i-adapter, shadow-peft); (iv) composition and unified frameworks (adapterfusion, adapterdrop, mam-adapter, unipelt, adamix); (v) output-level adapters for CLIP (clip-adapter, tip-adapter); (vi) gated prompt-adapters (llama-adapter, llama-adapter-v2). HF PEFT (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29) implements only two members of this family: LLaMA-Adapter (AdaptionPromptConfig) and ShadowPEFT (ShadowConfig); bottleneck adapters live in the AdapterHub 'adapters' library instead: DoubleSeqBnConfig = Houlsby, SeqBnConfig = Pfeiffer, ParBnConfig = parallel adapter, AdapterPlusConfig = Adapter+, SeqBnInvConfig/DoubleSeqBnInvConfig = MAD-X invertible adapters, CompacterConfig/CompacterPlusPlusConfig, MAMConfig (prefix bottleneck 800 + ParBn), UniPELTConfig (LoRA r=8, prefix length 10, SeqBn reduction 16, all gated; noted by AdapterHub as slightly different from the paper), and composition blocks Stack/Fuse/Split/BatchSplit/Parallel/Average. Overlaps with other families: llama-adapter also appears in the prompts family (same id, aligned to modification_kind input-or-activation-augmentation); adapterfusion and adamix could also be filed under composition/routing; repadapter is mergeable and, after merging, is a constrained LoRA-type additive update (B tied to W_0, shared across Q/K/V, plus a bias shift). residual-adapter is likewise exactly mergeable at inference. Boundary cases included deliberately: controlnet, t2i-adapter and ip-adapter are conditioning adapters/side networks for diffusion (they add a new input modality rather than re-target a task; ControlNet's trainable copy is not small), and k-adapter fine-tunes the backbone downstream (knowledge infusion). Year field is the first-version year of the listed arXiv record (the published version). Earlier preprints with different titles exist for mona (arXiv:2311.15010, Nov 2023) and tip-adapter (arXiv:2111.03930, Nov 2021). Code-level details verified from official repositories: Convpass, ST-Adapter, RepAdapter zero-init; LLaMA-Adapter V2 code applies the scale to the input (W(s*x)+b) whereas the paper writes s(Wx+b). Compacter does not state an exact identity-at-init guarantee. Mona's official code is not identity at init (default-initialized up-projection). Res-Tuning has no standalone repository; it is implemented in ModelScope SWIFT (ResTuningConfig). Considered but omitted for low uptake or being better placed elsewhere: PALs (Stickland & Murray, ICML 2019), CIAT parallel adapter for MT (Zhu et al. 2021), SparseAdapter (EMNLP Findings 2022), Quantized Side Tuning (ACL 2024), Hyperdecoders, Hyper-X, Polytropon (routing family), AdapterSoup (merging family), SSF and (IA)^3 (scaling family), Rebuffi et al. 2018 parallel residual adapters (folded into residual-adapter), Tiny-Attention adapter, Kronecker adapters (KronA), MoSA, E^3VA, DTL, UniPT, Side4Video, SAM-Adapter (application).
verification_summary: Adversarially verified on 2026-10-01: 31 methods and 10 papers, none dropped. All 41 arXiv ids (plus 1803.10082, 2311.15010, 2111.03930) were batch-checked against the arXiv API for title, first author and first-version year. Venues were confirmed via arXiv comments/journal-ref, Crossref DOIs (ECAI, AAAI, CVPR 2025, IJCV, ECCV, ACL Findings, Nature MI) and Semantic Scholar (TMLR, ICLR 2023; arXiv-only for RepAdapter, IP-Adapter, LLaMA-Adapter V2, ShadowPEFT). Every formula and parameter count was re-checked against the arXiv HTML/PDF full text, and the official code was read where init or parametrization was in doubt. HF PEFT claims were checked against huggingface/peft main (v0.21.1, 2026-09-29): only AdaptionPromptConfig and ShadowConfig belong to this family. 30 corrections in total. Key fixes: residual-adapter mergeable conditional -> yes; AdaMix training parameters (M+1)rd (shared up-projection); Pfeiffer residual made explicit; AIM joint adapter has no skip; Mona not identity at init in official code; RepAdapter W_d dense / W_u group-wise; Mona year 2024 and Tip-Adapter year 2022 (to match the listed arXiv ids); Convpass authors 'Jie and Deng'; Res-Tuning code in ModelScope SWIFT; four unjustified relations removed (residual-adapter->repadapter, repadapter->residual-adapter, llama-adapter->parallel-adapter, ip-adapter->llama-adapter) and RepAdapter-LoRA retyped as competes-with.
